topic: Generic uniform-single-door identification of direct effects from an LDiffPC partial difference graph, using two positive linear-Gaussian acyclic SCMs, invariant innovation variances, the population covariance pair, and a complete equality/sepset ledger, with component certificates, orientation-SAT/separator algorithms, fixed-treewidth complexity, symbolic same-component countermodels, boundary-honest confidence unions, a three-variable collider witness, and the ovarian-cancer BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B consumer.

open_problems.open_problem: On every CI-free irreducible component of an invariant-noise LDiffPC covariance-pair/equality-ledger model, is the direct-effect triple (α1, α2, α1-α2) generically identified only when the ledger forces zero or admits one single-door set valid in every compatible completion?

source_refs.claim: LDiffPC recovers difference structure through equality tests of conditional regression coefficients under diff-separation and diff-faithfulness, but does not give a componentwise direct-effect identification frontier for its partial output.
source_refs.author: Daria Bystrova and Emilie Devijver

source_refs.claim: For a given difference graph, Assaad characterizes direct-effect identification that is trivial or uses a common single-door set; the ovarian-cancer example identifies the linear BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B direct effect but not its total effect. The partial-ledger, algebraic-component lift is not covered.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 275

source_refs.claim: Computer-algebra elimination can classify a linear-SEM effect as identified, generically identified, or non-generically identified, including exhaustive small-graph analyses, but does not treat paired LDiffPC ledger models.
source_refs.author: Luis David Garcia-Puente, Sarah Spielvogel, and Seth Sullivant
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence

source_refs.excerpt: dependent-latent robustness, and direct-effect-coefficient identification remain open.
a sound pointwise response-function/CAD decision theorem

open_problems.why_unsolved: Assaad's iff result quantifies over SCMs compatible with a fully specified difference graph, whereas LDiffPC leaves orientations unresolved and supplies additional regression-equality and invariant-noise equations. Those equations split the compatible set into algebraic components on which completion-specific predecessor regressions might coincide for non-graphical reasons. The local LiNGAM and labeled-missingness runs respectively leave coefficient identification open and provide only pointwise fiber/CAD constancy. The missing necessity step is therefore to show that, after saturating by positivity and declared CI disequalities, absence of a component-uniform single-door set produces two admissible orders whose target-regression difference numerator is outside the component's radical ideal; graphical nonexistence alone does not establish this.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A componentwise necessary-and-sufficient generic-identification theorem giving αe = r_e(Y,X|W) on forced-zero or completion-uniform-single-door components and, on rejection, a radical nonmembership certificate plus two positive same-component SCM families with identical covariance pairs and ledger but different target triples.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from learned mechanism differences to the downstream question of whether the difference graph supports causal reasoning, and its formulation already quantifies over compatible SCM pairs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: difference graphs summarize cross-population mechanism changes -> representation alone does not answer causal-effect queries -> common single-door criteria identify direct effects on a given difference graph -> partial LDiffPC ledgers require a generic componentwise completeness frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Augment the polynomial covariance parametrization by a target coordinate, eliminate structural parameters, and decide generic fiber constancy through the target's elimination polynomial and radical membership.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is generic identification of a direct-effect coordinate from rational covariance data under paired equality constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode equal error variances and equal coefficients as colored-DAG rational constraints, recover parameters through predecessor regressions, and use the algebraic-manifold description to control equality varieties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An LDiffPC ledger is a paired colored Gaussian-DAG model whose cross-environment homogeneity constraints determine the compatible component geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Perturb or resample discovery statistics, screen candidate graphs, and union graph-specific regression-effect intervals while proving asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After componentwise identification reduces the target to a regression functional, this provides a concrete route from uncertain constraint-based discovery to valid inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the irreducible compatible-ledger components and all target-regression constancy failures be decided exactly from rational covariance inputs, with constructive positive SCM countermodel families rather than a numerical feasibility oracle?

source_refs.excerpt: Turn the certificate handle into an explicit semialgebraic decision procedure with input encoding
The symbolic CAD wrapper merely partitions the observed-cell parameter space

open_problems.why_unsolved: BACKSHIFT reviewers repeatedly identified the unencoded feasibility oracle as the missing algorithmic contribution, while the labeled-missingness run warns that CAD partitioning cannot replace a structural completeness proof. For LDiffPC, the first proof step changes to primary decomposition of paired invariant-noise ordered-Cholesky ideals, saturation by positivity and ledger disequalities, and radical membership tests for competing regression numerators. A negative answer must then be compiled into positive Gaussian SCM families on the same component, not left as a floating numerical witness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating sound-and-complete symbolic procedure with a rational input encoding, component ideals, degree-sensitive complexity bounds, radical membership or nonmembership certificates, and explicit positive same-covariance SCM parameter families realizing different direct-effect triples whenever constancy fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its equivalent-condition-to-constructive-solver arc is a close presentation model for an algebraic causal-identification decision problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: population matrices satisfy hidden structural equations -> equivalent algebraic conditions make feasibility decidable -> a constructive solver returns the latent representation -> LDiffPC requires componentwise identification and countermodel certificates

method_exemplars.technique: Apply effective quantifier elimination and sign-invariant semialgebraic decomposition with explicit dependence on variable count, polynomial count, and degree.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Positivity, covariance equations, ledger equalities, and CI disequalities form exactly such a semialgebraic decision input.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode observational compatibility and causal-query separation polynomially, then extract two feasible structural models when the query varies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The rejection certificate likewise requires exact same-observed structural models with separated causal targets, specialized to Gaussian Cholesky maps.

method_exemplars.technique: Linearize matrix-identification equations and relate target perturbation to a quantitative uniqueness modulus.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact component certificate needs a stability and inference rung when empirical covariances replace rational population inputs.

open_problems.open_problem: Can completion-uniform single-door identification from an LDiffPC equality/sepset ledger be decided in f(tw)·poly(p,L) time without enumerating all compatible order pairs, with checkable positive-SCM countermodels on rejection?

source_refs.claim: LDiffPC is a PC-style recovery algorithm driven by regression-coefficient equality tests, but does not supply a downstream query algorithm over all compatible completions.
source_refs.author: Daria Bystrova and Emilie Devijver

source_refs.claim: Assaad characterizes common-single-door identification on a given difference graph, while efficient effect-querying over a partial LDiffPC ledger and covariance-compatible order pairs lies outside the result.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 275

source_refs.claim: Adjustment validity can be reduced to separator search, with efficient testing and construction of adjustment sets for standard causal graph inputs.
source_refs.author: Benito van der Zander, Maciej Liskiewicz, and Johannes Textor

source_refs.claim: The half-trek criterion supplies polynomial-time sufficient certificates and a necessary obstruction for generic linear-SEM identifiability, illustrating certificate-driven identification without exhaustive elimination.
source_refs.author: Rina Foygel, Jan Draisma, and Mathias Drton

source_refs.excerpt: use MPDAG/PAG enumeration only as input to an econometric inference or efficiency question
The explicit bound proves finite termination and makes no polynomial-time claim.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing separator algorithms assume a fixed DAG, MAG, or standard equivalence-class graph, while an LDiffPC state must simultaneously satisfy orientations, two covariance factorizations, cross-environment innovation-variance equalities, regression equalities, and recorded sepsets. The failed MPDAG run confirms that graph-only effect invariance is already characterized, so the new state cannot merely enumerate ordinary completions. The first missing step is a tree-decomposition dynamic program whose bags carry orientation, uniform-separator legality, ledger consistency, and enough algebraic information to witness a nonzero target-difference polynomial; it is not known whether this summary is bounded solely by skeleton treewidth.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An f(tw)·poly(p,L)-time sound-and-complete algorithm returning either a set W proved single-door-valid for X-to-Y in every covariance-compatible completion, a forced-zero certificate, or two symbolic positive SCM families on one CI-free component with equal observables and unequal target coefficients.

writing_exemplar.why: Its PC-style narrative naturally motivates a second, query-specific algorithm whose input is the equality and sepset record produced during discovery.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: two related environments make full graph recovery wasteful -> equality tests learn the difference structure directly -> LDiffPC records local equality and separator information -> causal use requires an efficient query algorithm over all compatible completions

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce adjustment validity to separation in a proper back-door subgraph and use constructive separator algorithms to test and enumerate admissible sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The accepting certificate is likewise a uniformly valid separator after deleting the target edge; the new work lifts the reduction through paired completions and ledger constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Compress rational-identification equations into a locally checkable graphical certificate based on no-sided-intersection trek systems, with small-graph algebraic audits of the remaining gap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It models how an expensive generic-identification question can become a graph certificate while retaining an algebraic rejection audit.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace global DAG enumeration by local valid parent-set enumeration and prove consistency of the resulting collection of regression-based causal-effect estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The output is likewise a completion-indexed collection of regression coefficients, making IDA the nearest estimator blueprint for avoiding global order enumeration.

open_problems.open_problem: How can one construct a confidence union for the two-environment direct-effect triple selected through LDiffPC that is uniformly honest as regression-equality, conditional-independence, and competing-regression margins jointly approach zero?

source_refs.claim: LDiffPC selects its graph and ledger using equality tests of conditional regression coefficients, making the reported structure unstable near equality boundaries.
source_refs.author: Daria Bystrova and Emilie Devijver

source_refs.claim: Test inversion gives confidence regions for total effects under unknown equal-variance Gaussian DAG structure, accounting jointly for graph and coefficient uncertainty, but does not treat paired equality ledgers or direct-effect vectors.
source_refs.author: David Strieder and Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Repeated perturbed PC runs followed by unions of graph-specific intervals yield asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after constraint-based discovery, but not after two-environment equality-ledger selection.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Zijian Guo, and Daniel Malinsky

source_refs.claim: Randomized causal discovery enables valid post-discovery inference and shows that treating a learned graph as fixed can severely undercover, but it does not handle LDiffPC's paired equality and CI selection events.
source_refs.author: Paula Gradu, Tijana Zrnic, Yixin Wang, and Michael I. Jordan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 120(550)

source_refs.excerpt: operator-norm contraction of the confidence union remains the first-class open question.
a fixed-branch Wald interval after extremal reporting has nonuniform conditional coverage
Name one discovery rule, preferably PC-stable with Fisher-z partial-correlation tests

open_problems.why_unsolved: The target is nonregular at three boundaries at once: a small cross-environment coefficient difference changes the equality ledger, a small partial correlation changes the sepset and CI component, and a small difference between completion-specific regressions changes whether the target is a singleton. Strieder-Drton invert single-environment homoscedastic-DAG tests for total effects, while Chang-Guo-Malinsky screen graphs chosen by CI tests. The BACKSHIFT and rejected IDA runs independently leave contraction and branch-boundary coverage unresolved. None of these arguments jointly handles two covariance samples, equality-test selection, irreducible-component changes, and a three-coordinate direct-effect target, so ordinary intervals around the selected regression condition on the wrong discrete model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A test-inverted random closed-set confidence union for (α1, α2, α1-α2) over every covariance pair, ledger, and component not rejected by joint equality-and-CI tests, with a uniform liminf coverage theorem over local boundary sequences, an explicit Hausdorff contraction rate under positive separation, and set-valued output or abstention at zero separation.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames structure and numerical effect uncertainty as inseparable and motivates test inversion instead of treating a learned graph as fixed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: unknown causal structure is learned from the same data -> fixed-graph effect intervals ignore model-choice uncertainty -> joint structure-and-effect tests are inverted -> extend inversion to two-environment equality ledgers and a direct-effect triple

method_exemplars.technique: Invert constrained or split likelihood-ratio tests jointly over causal orders and a fixed-effect restriction, with combinatorial pruning of implausible orders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired confidence set likewise tests a causal-effect restriction while treating compatible Gaussian structures as nuisance models.

method_exemplars.technique: Perturb discovery test statistics, retain a screened family of graphs, and union graph-specific effect intervals to cover a fixed population effect after PC selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: LDiffPC is PC-like but selects on equality as well as CI tests, so the screening-union proof is the nearest modular route to valid post-LDiffPC inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Randomize the discovery rule and calibrate subsequent inference through the resulting stability guarantee, retaining more data than simple splitting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an alternative proof architecture if direct inversion of the equality-ledger selection event is too irregular.

open_problems.open_problem: Which coordinates of the environment-specific direct-effect triple remain generically identifiable when full cross-environment innovation-variance invariance is weakened to known invariant blocks or an unknown sparse set of variance changes?

source_refs.claim: Difference-DAG support can be identified under topological-layering conditions despite unequal and changing Gaussian noise variances, but the target is changed-edge support rather than numerical direct-effect coordinates.
source_refs.author: Vineet Malik, Kevin Bello, Asish Ghoshal, and Jean Honorio
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 40th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 244

source_refs.claim: Partial homoscedasticity yields a CPDAG representation and an efficient construction algorithm for distributional equivalence classes between arbitrary-variance and fully homoscedastic Gaussian DAGs.
source_refs.author: Jun Wu and Mathias Drton
source_refs.venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory 4

source_refs.claim: DCI learns differences between two Gaussian DAG models sharing a topological order through regression and residual-variance invariance tests, under assumptions designed for sparse changes.
source_refs.author: Yuhao Wang, Chandler Squires, Anastasiya Belyaeva, and Caroline Uhler
source_refs.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31

source_refs.claim: Colored Gaussian DAG models encode partial equality of error variances and structural coefficients as rational covariance constraints and study their geometry and structural identifiability.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, and Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 88(3)

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available methods resolve complementary objects: Malik et al. recover change support with varying variances, Wu-Drton characterize a one-law partial-homoscedastic equivalence class, DCI tests sparse changes, and colored-DAG geometry handles within-model equality constraints. None characterizes effect-coordinate identification from a two-law partial difference ledger when only some innovations are invariant. The first proof step that changes is the Cholesky compatibility ideal: instead of equating every innovation-variance rational function across environments, it contains equalities only on named blocks or a union over sparse change supports, allowing order reversals excluded by full invariance to re-enter. Searches combining partial homoscedasticity, difference graphs, and direct-effect identification located these separate strands but no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A block-indexed componentwise frontier characterizing whether α1, α2, α1-α2, or only a finite identified set is determined, with rational formulas for identified coordinates and positive same-observable countermodels for every nonidentified coordinate.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates robustness to changing noise variances through the practical goal of learning causal changes without identifying either full DAG.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: scientific comparisons seek changed mechanisms rather than two full graphs -> strict noise invariance is often implausible -> layering can preserve support recovery under variance changes -> determine which numerical direct effects survive partial invariance

method_exemplars.technique: Represent groupwise equal-error-variance distributional equivalence by a partially oriented graph and characterize legal edge reversals through equal-variance blocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Known invariant blocks across two environments create the analogous intermediate equivalence class between unconstrained and fully invariant noise.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate equality colors into rational covariance equations using predecessor regressions and residual variances, then analyze the resulting algebraic model geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blockwise cross-environment innovation invariances are colored parameter equalities on a paired Gaussian-DAG model.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert structure-and-effect tests under partial homoscedasticity to build mathematically valid confidence regions for total causal effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the blockwise frontier identifies a direct-effect coordinate, the same nuisance-order inversion can supply its inference rung and quantify the cost of weaker variance invariance.

literature_map:
1. Bystrova and Devijver (2026, arXiv:2606.13947) introduce diff-separation, diff-faithfulness, and LDiffPC based on conditional-regression equality tests; the contribution is discovery-first, not a componentwise causal-query theory.
2. Assaad (2025, CLeaR/PMLR 275, arXiv:2411.01292) gives iff conditions for direct effects on a given difference graph when identification is trivial or uses a common single-door set; his ovarian-cancer example identifies the linear BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B direct effect but not the total effect.
3. Wang, Squires, Belyaeva, and Uhler (2018, NeurIPS, arXiv:1802.05631) directly estimate sparse causal-graph differences under a shared topological order using regression and residual-variance invariances.
4. Malik, Bello, Ghoshal, and Honorio (2024, UAI/PMLR 244) identify difference-DAG support under topological layering even with unequal or changing Gaussian noise variances, but not numerical effect triples.
5. Peters and Buehlmann (2014, Biometrika, arXiv:1205.2536) establish full DAG identifiability under equal Gaussian error variances, the single-law endpoint behind variance-based orientation.
6. Wu and Drton (2023, IEEE JSAIT, arXiv:2308.08959) characterize the intermediate partial-homoscedastic equivalence class and construct its CPDAG efficiently.
7. Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026, JRSSB, arXiv:2404.04024) encode coefficient and variance equalities in colored Gaussian DAGs and prove geometric and structural-identifiability results.
8. Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010, UAI, arXiv:1007.3784) provide elimination tests for generic causal-effect identification and exhaustive three- and four-node audits.
9. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1107.5552) turn generic linear-SEM identifiability into graphical half-trek certificates, while retaining a sufficient-versus-necessary gap.
10. Perkovic (2020, UAI/PMLR 124, arXiv:1910.02997) gives a necessary-and-sufficient effect-identification criterion for MPDAGs, illustrating completeness over partial orientations without cross-environment equality ledgers.
11. Perkovic et al. (2018, JMLR, arXiv:1507.01524) and van der Zander, Liskiewicz, and Textor (2019, Artificial Intelligence) give complete adjustment/separator criteria and efficient construction in standard graph classes.
12. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buehlmann (2009, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0810.4214) avoid global CPDAG enumeration through local parent-set enumeration and consistently estimate collections of regression effects.
13. Strieder and Drton (2023, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:2309.04298) invert joint structure-and-effect tests under equal-variance Gaussian SEMs, but target single-environment total effects.
14. Gradu et al. (2025, JASA, arXiv:2208.05949) and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2026, Biometrika, arXiv:2405.06763) repair post-discovery undercoverage through randomized or screening-union methods; neither treats two-environment equality selection.
15. The central tension is that graphical common-single-door completeness is known for a given difference graph, while LDiffPC's partial equality ledger adds algebraic information that may identify effect coordinates componentwise beyond graph-only criteria.
